---
title: "Building ComptoxR from schemas"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  eval = FALSE
)
```

Most of ComptoxR's exported wrappers are generated. The
[`specmill`](https://github.com/seanthimons/specmill) toolkit reads the saved
production OpenAPI schemas and a set of YAML files that say which operations
to wrap and how, then writes one `R/<wrapper>.R` file per operation, its
roxygen documentation, and its offline contract tests. This article walks
through that pipeline end to end for maintainers. Branches, CI and releases are
covered in [Development lifecycle](development-lifecycle.html); test lanes are
in
[`dev/TESTING_GUIDE.md`](https://github.com/seanthimons/ComptoxR/blob/main/dev/TESTING_GUIDE.md);
every maintainer script is indexed in
[`dev/README.md`](https://github.com/seanthimons/ComptoxR/blob/main/dev/README.md).

```
schema/*_prod.json  ─┐
specmill.yml         ├─>  generate_specmill.R --apply  ─>  R/<wrapper>.R
apis/<service>.yml   │                                     tests/testthat/
inst/hook_config.yml │                                     .specmill/manifest.json
dev/*_callbacks.R   ─┘                 devtools::document()  ─>  man/, NAMESPACE
```

Run every command below from the package root.

## 1. Install the pinned toolkit

Specmill is a development dependency only; installed ComptoxR does not need it.
The exact revision is pinned in `dev/specmill-lock.json` (version, source
commit and source-archive SHA-256). `install_specmill()` archives that commit
from a local Specmill checkout, checks the archive hash, and installs it into
the ignored `dev/specmill-pilot/artifacts/toolkit-library/<version>/`.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/seanthimons/specmill ../specmill  # once
Rscript dev/install_specmill.R   # or set SPECMILL_SOURCE_REPO to another checkout
```

Point `R_LIBS` at the versioned library so every script, and every R process
it starts, finds the pinned toolkit:

```bash
export R_LIBS="$PWD/dev/specmill-pilot/artifacts/toolkit-library/$(Rscript -e 'cat(jsonlite::read_json("dev/specmill-lock.json")$version)')"
```

Also install [Air](https://posit-dev.github.io/air/) 0.11.0 (the formatter
pinned in `specmill.yml`; generated code is formatted with it and CI compares
byte for byte) and roxygen2 8.1.x (`Config/roxygen2/version` in
`DESCRIPTION`; older roxygen2 rewrites all of `man/`).

## 2. Refresh the production schemas

Saved schemas live in `schema/` as `<service>_prod.json`. Three functions
download them from the approved production servers:

```r
pkgload::load_all()
ct_schema()     # CompTox Dashboard: ctx_chemical, ctx_hazard, ctx_bioactivity, ctx_exposure
chemi_schema()  # Cheminformatics services
epi_schema()    # EPI Suite (drops the volatile x-epi-health block before saving)
```

You rarely need to run these by hand. The **Schema Update Check** workflow
runs them on a schedule, regenerates everything below, and opens an
`automated/schema-update` PR when a schema changed (see
[Scheduled automation](development-lifecycle.html#scheduled-automation)).
Schema files are hashed into `.specmill/manifest.json`, so a changed schema
must always be followed by `--apply`.

PubChem has no production schema. Its wrappers come from the first-party
overlay `schema/pubchem-reviewed.json`, which is edited by hand.

## 3. Say what to wrap: `specmill.yml` and `apis/`

`specmill.yml` holds project-wide settings: the request helper
(`.ct_request`), the CTX credential (`ctx_api_key`), the formatter, the list of
service files, and the callback files.

Selection is **opt-out**. Every GET and POST operation in a listed schema is
generated unless a `selection.exclude` rule in `specmill.yml` matches it, or
the group narrows itself with `selection.include` (as `pubchem` and
`chemi_classyfire` do). Each
rule is a path regex, optionally prefixed with a method (`'POST ^/api/stdizer/?$'`)
to exclude that method only. Comment each rule with the reason or issue
number.

Each schema has one file, `apis/<service>.yml`:

- `schemas.files` names the saved schema.
- `defaults` holds service-wide settings, such as CTX batching
  (`max_items: 100`, `split: true`, `on_error: drop`).
- `groups.<service>.names` maps every route to its wrapper name. Names follow
  the path in snake_case with a `ct_`, `chemi_` or `epi_` prefix; a POST that
  shares a GET's path gets `_bulk`. Any departure from that default carries a
  `# why` comment.
- `groups.<service>.operations` holds per-operation settings: server
  resolver, response policy, input forms, batching, pagination, docs and
  request arguments. Each entry has a `# why:` line saying what behaviour it
  keeps.

[`dev/specmill-333/SELECTION.md`](https://github.com/seanthimons/ComptoxR/blob/main/dev/specmill-333/SELECTION.md)
records the naming rules, the non-default groups, and every deferral in
detail.

### Hooks and callbacks

Behaviour that YAML can't express lives in ComptoxR, not in generated files:

- **Runtime hooks** (`R/hooks_*.R`), wired to wrappers by name in
  `inst/hook_config.yml`. `Rscript dev/check_hook_config.R` validates that
  file.
- **Generation callbacks** (`dev/specmill_callbacks.R`,
  `dev/specmill_pubchem_callbacks.R`), named by `prepare:` and similar keys in
  the API files.
- **The native request helper** `R/z_specmill_request.R`, emitted from the
  pinned toolkit by `dev/specmill-342/emit.R` and checked in CI by
  `dev/specmill-342/verify.R`.

## 4. Generate

```bash
Rscript dev/generate_specmill.R --plan    # preview; changes nothing
Rscript dev/generate_specmill.R --apply   # write wrappers, tests and manifest
Rscript -e 'devtools::document()'        # man/ and NAMESPACE
Rscript dev/generate_specmill.R --apply   # again, so the manifest records man/ and NAMESPACE
Rscript dev/generate_specmill.R --check   # must exit 0
```

Read the `--plan` output before applying. Generation refuses to run while the
plan reports signature **drift** (a wrapper's arguments would change) or an
unsupported operation. Review the change; deleting the old `R/` file clears
drift for a deliberate rename.

`.specmill/manifest.json` records a hash of every owned output **and every
package input**, including all of `R/`, `schema/`, the hooks and the
callbacks. Any edit to those files, even a hand-written utility, makes the
manifest stale, and the **Specmill Maintenance** check fails with "Generated
output is stale or protected". Fix it by running `--apply` and committing the
manifest. That check also regenerates from scratch and fails on any changed or
new file, so never hand-edit a generated wrapper: change the YAML, hook or
callback and regenerate.

Operation lifecycle flags:

```bash
# Placeholders: substitute a real service id, method and path.
# Defer an operation whose production schema is broken (reason is recorded)
Rscript dev/generate_specmill.R --apply --enroll="<service> <METHOD> <path>=<reason>"
# Lift a deferral
Rscript dev/generate_specmill.R --apply --clear="<service> <METHOD> <path>"
# Remove the generated output of a retired operation
Rscript dev/generate_specmill.R --apply --prune="<service> <METHOD> <path>"
```

Deferred operations are retried automatically when their schema fingerprint
changes.

## 5. Tests

Specmill writes offline contract tests for the wrappers it generates. Their
fixed request contracts live in
`tests/testthat/fixtures/specmill-contracts.rds`. `dev/generate_tests.R` is
the one remaining legacy generator; it covers exported wrappers whose tests
Specmill doesn't write, from `test_args:` in `inst/hook_config.yml`.

```bash
Rscript dev/detect_test_gaps.R          # wrappers without tests
Rscript dev/generate_tests.R --generate
Rscript dev/generate_tests.R --check
Rscript dev/unit_test_readiness_audit.R --check-exports --fail-on-gaps
```

The readiness audit regenerates `dev/reports/unit_test_readiness_audit.json`;
commit it when it changes. `dev/export_test_exclusions.json` lists exports
deliberately without tests, and `dev/vcr_test_classification.json` classifies
any test that uses a cassette. Live recording is opt-in and needs a real
`ctx_api_key`; see `dev/TESTING_GUIDE.md`.

## 6. Check before you push

```bash
Rscript dev/generate_specmill.R --check
Rscript dev/check_hook_config.R
Rscript dev/check_public_api.R   # public code and docs use production APIs only
Rscript dev/cran_readiness.R     # CRAN-safe lane: no key, no network, no databases
```

`dev/update_coverage.R --apply` refreshes the schema coverage badges from
`dev/coverage.yml` when the set of wrapped operations changes.

## What stays hand-written

- **Client utilities**: the `*_server()` selectors, `run_setup()`,
  `run_verbose()`, `run_debug()`, `batch_limit()` and the `util_*` helpers.
- **Local database clients**: the `dss_*`, `eco_*` and `toxval_*` functions
  and their Plumber servers.
- **`ct_related()` and `ct_similar()`**: they call dashboard routes that no
  production schema describes, and call `.ct_request()` directly.
- **Deferred operations**: ten operations, listed in `SELECTION.md`, have no
  wrapper until their production schemas are fixed.

If Specmill can't express a feature, or can't reproduce an existing wrapper's
behaviour, **fix it upstream**. Open an issue in
[seanthimons/specmill](https://github.com/seanthimons/specmill/issues) (or
comment on the open Specmill PR that is meant to fix it) with the wrapper, the
operation (method, path and schema file), what the old wrapper did versus what
Specmill produces, and a minimal reproduction. Leave the wrapper on its
current implementation until the fix is released and the pin is updated. Do
not work around a gap with a hand-written wrapper or a patched helper.

## Updating the Specmill pin

1. Edit `dev/specmill-lock.json`: `version`, `source_commit`, and
   `source_archive_sha256` (from `git archive --format=tar <commit> | sha256sum`).
2. `Rscript dev/install_specmill.R` and re-export `R_LIBS` for the new
   version.
3. Re-emit the native helper. In R, `source("dev/specmill-342/emit.R")` and
   run `emit_issue342(mode = "check")`. If it fails, review the new helper
   and run `emit_issue342(mode = "apply")`. When the helper code itself
   changed, also pass
   `adopt = <SHA-256 of the current R/z_specmill_request.R>`. This rewrites `R/z_specmill_request.R` and
   `.specmill/helpers/.ct_request.json`.
4. Record the adoption in `dev/specmill-342/adoption.json`: append the
   existing `current_adoption` to `adoption_history`, then set a new
   `current_adoption` whose `toolkit` is an exact copy of
   `dev/specmill-lock.json` and whose `adopted_sha256` holds the new hashes of
   `R/z_specmill_request.R` and `dev/specmill-342/emit.R`. Add a short
   `review` note.
5. `Rscript dev/specmill-342/verify.R` must pass; it checks both the lock
   match and the helper hash.
6. Run steps 4 to 6 above. Expect every generated file's header and the
   manifest to change.
7. Commit the lock, `adoption.json`, the helper and its
   `.specmill/helpers/` record, the manifest and the regenerated output
   together. To roll back, restore the previous pin and its matching output
   together.

## A separate local client

Development or staging schemas, and clients generated from them, stay outside
every public ComptoxR checkout. To build one, source
`dev/generate_local_client.R` and call `generate_local_client()` with explicit
input and output roots, a schema file, a base URL, and a distinct package
name; `dev/verify_local_client.R` checks the result. See
[`dev/LOCAL_CLIENTS.md`](https://github.com/seanthimons/ComptoxR/blob/main/dev/LOCAL_CLIENTS.md).
To promote an operation into ComptoxR, regenerate it here from its approved
production schema; never copy a local client's files into the package.
